title: Made at twilight (Avot 5:6)
hookLine: ten things were made at dusk before the first Shabbat: the rainbow, the manna, the staff, the letters
tomorrow: what do the wise say when they just don't know?

cards: Phones come up at sunset. Golden hour: the light that makes an ordinary street look like something's about to happen. Avot has its own golden hour.
Creation's sixth day is ending; the first Shabbat is about to begin. And in that thin light, between day and night, the mishnah says God made ten more things. Not stars or seas.
Strange, specific things that turn up much later in the story.

teach.h: A DONKEY'S MOUTH, A RAINBOW, MANNA.
teach.b: The list: the mouth of the earth that swallowed Korah's rebels. The mouth of the well in the wilderness. The mouth of Balaam's donkey, which talks.
The rainbow. The manna, the bread from heaven. Moses's staff.
The shamir, which tradition says could cut stone. The writing, the engraving, and the tablets. Some add more: Abraham's ram, Moses's grave.
And some say tongs, made with tongs. That one's worth telling a friend tonight. Tongs are made by holding hot metal with tongs.
So who held the first pair? The answer: they were made at twilight. Look at the list again and a pattern shows.
Nearly everything on it breaks the ordinary rules later on. Donkeys don't talk; bread doesn't fall from the sky. The mishnah's answer is that these weren't patches added in a hurry.
They were made at the edge of creation, ready and waiting.
Maimonides reads it that way in his commentary: the wonders were built into the world from the start. And why at twilight?
The Hebrew is bein hashmashot, the in-between hour, not quite day, not quite night. The rabbis treat it as an edge, hard to rule on.
The things that cross the line between ordinary and wonder were made in the hour that sits on a line.

how: Shabbat begins at sunset on Friday, and Shabbat candles are lit shortly before; the twilight list of Avot 5:6 is studied on summer Shabbat afternoons with the rest of chapter five.

games.q: your little brother asks: was the rainbow invented after Noah's flood?
o: Avot says it was made at twilight before the first Shabbat, then shows up as a sign after the flood.
yes: Avot says God made it brand new once the rain stopped, as a promise.
Avot doesn't mention it; the rainbow appears only in the story of Noah.
games.why: the rainbow is on the twilight list in Avot 5:6. in Genesis it appears as a sign after the flood; the mishnah says it was waiting all along.

practice: Find the nearest edge of light: a window, a lamp, the line where a wall goes from bright to shadow, even on your own hand. Rest your eyes right on that edge, and don't decide whether it's light or dark.
If it's dusk where you are, look at the sky instead, and watch it change a little with each breath.
